Subject: Hyperlane renewal & capacity uplift — draft redlines attached

Samir — great talking yesterday. Per our call, I’m circling back with the renewal paperwork for your review. We’ve captured the 18-month term, the 2.5x committed capacity uplift, and the proposed blended rate. Please find attached: the draft Order Form with the new capacity schedule and an MSA amendment showing the term shift.

Key asks from your side we recalled:
- Data residency confirmation for EU workloads (you flagged some cross-region traffic)
- Clarification on the SLA credit calculation for burst capacity
- A clean migration window for cutover in September

I’ve looped in Lauren to help Fast-track any legal clarifications — she’s included in case we need narrow redlines. Next step: can you share your redlines by EOD Wednesday so we can get Legal to respond Thursday?

Attachments: Hyperlane_Renewal_Orderform_v1_redline.docx (order form, redline view), Hyperlane_MSA_Amendment_Redline.pdf (MSA amendment, tracked)

Thanks — excited to keep this moving.

—Dylan
Dylan Brooks
Account Exec, Redwood Inference

From: Samir Gupta <samir@hyperlane.ai>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Cc: Patricia Lee <patricia.legal@hyperlane.ai>, Alex Romero <alex.ops@hyperlane.ai>
Date: Wed, 15 Jul 2026 11:07:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Hyperlane renewal & capacity uplift — draft redlines attached

Dylan — thanks for the docs. Quick primer from our side after a legal ops review: Patricia and I marked a few areas we need changed before we can route to procurement. High level:

1) Term and termination: we need an option for a 12-month early termination right if material SLA misses (>1% downtime in a rolling 90-day period) — propose a partial refund for unused committed capacity.
2) Data residency: our EU customers must keep infer requests and logs in-region; we need language ensuring EU model inference and logs stay in EU unless we consent otherwise.
3) Audit rights: Patricia requested we narrow audit frequency to once per year and add a notice period.

I attached a redline of the Order Form with inline comments and a short cover note in the MSA PDF. We’re not trying to block this — just need those protections before we sign. Can we get legal input on these three bullets?

—Samir
Samir Gupta
Head of Platform, Hyperlane

Attachment: Hyperlane_Renewal_Orderform_v1_hyperlane_redline.docx

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Samir Gupta <samir@hyperlane.ai>, Patricia Lee <patricia.legal@hyperlane.ai>
Date: Thu, 16 Jul 2026 09:34:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Hyperlane renewal & capacity uplift — draft redlines attached

Team — I reviewed Hyperlane’s redlines. High-level takeaways:

• Termination language: we can’t broadly accept a unilateral 12-month early termination for any SLA slip — however, we can offer a defined SLA remediation path: if downtime >1% in 90 days, Redwood will provide pro-rata credits for affected committed capacity and a 90-day cure period before any termination right accrues.

• Data residency: we’ll accept a carve-out to commit EU inference and logs to EU regions for data tagged as EU-resident, with standard exceptions for disaster recovery. We need a concise definition for "EU-resident data" — suggest the customer-controlled flag in the order form.

• Audit rights: agree to annual audits with 30 days’ notice, and we’ll require any on-site audit to be scoped and cost-shared if intrusive.

I’ve prepared suggested language and added it to the attached PDF. Ben — please confirm the change to the SLA credit calc math with the infra team (how credits scale against burst usage).

Thanks, Lauren
Lauren Bishop
Sr. Legal Counsel, Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: Samir Gupta <samir@hyperlane.ai>
Date: Mon, 20 Jul 2026 10:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Hyperlane renewal & capacity uplift — draft redlines attached

Quick infra note on SLA credits: we can implement a two-tier credit calculation. Proposal:
- For committed capacity incidents (affecting baseline), credit = pro-rata percentage of committed spend for affected window.
- For burst capacity, credit is capped at 25% of the burst charges in the impacted billing period.

This preserves predictability for Hyperlane while limiting exposure. If Hyperlane wants higher cap on burst credits, we can propose a step-down pricing addendum to offset exposure.

I’ll update the order form numbers and include a worked example.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Head of Customer Success, Redwood Inference
